1	# Dot-com vs AI Bubble Comparison Dataset
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	Four datasets capturing key market metrics across two technology-driven market booms: the 1997–2002 dot-com era and the 2021–2024 AI era. The data is structured for side-by-side temporal alignment using a common `quarter_offset` or `year` field within each era.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### nasdaq_index
     9	Quarterly NASDAQ Composite closing values, rebased to 100 at the start of each era. Fields: `era` (string: "Dot-com" or "AI"), `quarter_offset` (integer 0–23), `label` (calendar quarter string), `index_value` (float). The dot-com series spans 24 quarters (1997-Q1 to 2002-Q4); the AI series spans 16 quarters (2021-Q1 to 2024-Q4).
    10	
    11	### pe_ratio
    12	Trailing 12-month P/E ratio for the NASDAQ Composite, sampled at irregular quarterly intervals. Fields: `era`, `quarter_offset`, `label`, `pe` (float, ratio). Dot-com P/E ranges from ~28 to ~105; AI-era P/E ranges from ~24 to ~40.
    13	
    14	### ipo_counts
    15	Annual count of technology-sector IPOs on US exchanges. Fields: `era`, `year` (integer), `ipo_count` (integer). Dot-com era: 6 years; AI era: 4 years.
    16	
    17	### corporate_earnings
    18	Aggregate annual net income for NASDAQ-100 companies in nominal billion USD. Fields: `era`, `year`, `earnings_bn` (float; may be negative). Dot-com earnings range from −12.3 to 30.5 B; AI-era earnings range from 358 to 510 B.
    19	
    20	## Data Notes
    21	- NASDAQ index values are rebased independently per era; absolute levels differ dramatically.
    22	- P/E ratios for the dot-com era include periods of near-zero aggregate earnings, inflating the ratio.
    23	- Nominal earnings are not inflation-adjusted; direct magnitude comparison across eras should note the ~20-year gap.
    24	- 2024 figures are estimates based on analyst consensus as of late 2024.

     6	
     7	# Data Visualization Skill
     8	
     9	Chart selection guidance, Python visualization code patterns, design principles, and accessibility considerations for creating effective data visualizations.
    10	
    11	## Chart Selection Guide
    12	
    13	### Choose by Data Relationship
    14	
    15	| What You're Showing | Best Chart | Alternatives |
    16	|---|---|---|
    17	| **Trend over time** | Line chart | Area chart (if showing cumulative or composition) |
    18	| **Comparison across categories** | Vertical bar chart | Horizontal bar (many categories), lollipop chart |
    19	| **Ranking** | Horizontal bar chart | Dot plot, slope chart (comparing two periods) |
    20	| **Part-to-whole composition** | Stacked bar chart | Treemap (hierarchical), waffle chart |
    21	| **Composition over time** | Stacked area chart | 100% stacked bar (for proportion focus) |
    22	| **Distribution** | Histogram | Box plot (comparing groups), violin plot, strip plot |
    23	| **Correlation (2 variables)** | Scatter plot | Bubble chart (add 3rd variable as size) |
    24	| **Correlation (many variables)** | Heatmap (correlation matrix) | Pair plot |
    25	| **Geographic patterns** | Choropleth map | Bubble map, hex map |
    26	| **Flow / process** | Sankey diagram | Funnel chart (sequential stages) |
    27	| **Relationship network** | Network graph | Chord diagram |
    28	| **Performance vs. target** | Bullet chart | Gauge (single KPI only) |
    29	| **Multiple KPIs at once** | Small multiples | Dashboard with separate charts |
    30	
    31	### When NOT to Use Certain Charts
    32	
    33	- **Pie charts**: Avoid unless <6 categories and exact proportions matter less than rough comparison. Humans are bad at comparing angles. Use bar charts instead.
    34	- **3D charts**: Never. They distort perception and add no information.
    35	- **Dual-axis charts**: Use cautiously. They can mislead by implying correlation. Clearly label both axes if used.
    36	- **Stacked bar (many categories)**: Hard to compare middle segments. Use small multiples or grouped bars instead.
    37	- **Donut charts**: Slightly better than pie charts but same fundamental issues. Use for single KPI display at most.
    38	
    39	## Python Visualization Code Patterns
    40	
    41	### Setup and Style
    42	
    43	```python
    44	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    45	import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
    46	import seaborn as sns
    47	import pandas as pd
    48	import numpy as np
    49	
    50	# Professional style setup
    51	plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
    52	plt.rcParams.update({
    53	    'figure.figsize': (10, 6),
    54	    'figure.dpi': 150,
    55	    'font.size': 11,
    56	    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    57	    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    58	    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    59	    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    60	    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    61	    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    62	    'figure.titlesize': 16,
    63	})
    64	
    65	# Colorblind-friendly palettes
    66	PALETTE_CATEGORICAL = ['#4C72B0', '#DD8452', '#55A868', '#C44E52', '#8172B3', '#937860']

   240	
   241	## Design Principles
   242	
   243	### Color
   244	
   245	- **Use color purposefully**: Color should encode data, not decorate
   246	- **Highlight the story**: Use a bright accent color for the key insight; grey everything else
   247	- **Sequential data**: Use a single-hue gradient (light to dark) for ordered values
   248	- **Diverging data**: Use a two-hue gradient with neutral midpoint for data with a meaningful center
   249	- **Categorical data**: Use distinct hues, maximum 6-8 before it gets confusing
   250	- **Avoid red/green only**: 8% of men are red-green colorblind. Use blue/orange as primary pair
   251	
   252	### Typography
   253	
   254	- **Title states the insight**: "Revenue grew 23% YoY" beats "Revenue by Month"
   255	- **Subtitle adds context**: Date range, filters applied, data source
   256	- **Axis labels are readable**: Never rotated 90 degrees if avoidable. Shorten or wrap instead
   257	- **Data labels add precision**: Use on key points, not every single bar
   258	- **Annotation highlights**: Call out specific points with text annotations
   259	
   260	### Layout
   261	
   262	- **Reduce chart junk**: Remove gridlines, borders, backgrounds that don't carry information
   263	- **Sort meaningfully**: Categories sorted by value (not alphabetically) unless there's a natural order (months, stages)
   264	- **Appropriate aspect ratio**: Time series wider than tall (3:1 to 2:1); comparisons can be squarer
   265	- **White space is good**: Don't cram charts together. Give each visualization room to breathe
   266	
   267	### Accuracy
   268	
   269	- **Bar charts start at zero**: Always. A bar from 95 to 100 exaggerates a 5% difference
   270	- **Line charts can have non-zero baselines**: When the range of variation is meaningful
   271	- **Consistent scales across panels**: When comparing multiple charts, use the same axis range
   272	- **Show uncertainty**: Error bars, confidence intervals, or ranges when data is uncertain
   273	- **Label your axes**: Never make the reader guess what the numbers mean
   274	
   275	## Accessibility Considerations
   276	
   277	### Color Blindness
   278	
   279	- Never rely on color alone to distinguish data series
   280	- Add pattern fills, different line styles (solid, dashed, dotted), or direct labels
   281	- Test with a colorblind simulator (e.g., Coblis, Sim Daltonism)
   282	- Use the colorblind-friendly palette: `sns.color_palette("colorblind")`
   283	
   284	### Screen Readers
   285	
   286	- Include alt text describing the chart's key finding
   287	- Provide a data table alternative alongside the visualization
   288	- Use semantic titles and labels
   289	
   290	### General Accessibility
   291	
   292	- Sufficient contrast between data elements and background
   293	- Text size minimum 10pt for labels, 12pt for titles
   294	- Avoid conveying information only through spatial position (add labels)
   295	- Consider printing: does the chart work in black and white?
   296	
   297	### Accessibility Checklist
   298	
   299	Before sharing a visualization:
   300	- [ ] Chart works without color (patterns, labels, or line styles differentiate series)
   301	- [ ] Text is readable at standard zoom level
   302	- [ ] Title describes the insight, not just the data
   303	- [ ] Axes are labeled with units
   304	- [ ] Legend is clear and positioned without obscuring data
   305	- [ ] Data source and date range are noted

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import numpy as np

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Professional editorial style setup
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.figsize': (14, 16),
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 13,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    'figure.titlesize': 15,
    'axes.linewidth': 0.8,
    'grid.linewidth': 0.4,
})

# Color palette
COLOR_DOTCOM = '#2E5C8A'
COLOR_AI = '#D95F43'
COLOR_DOTCOM_LIGHT = '#7BA3C8'
COLOR_AI_LIGHT = '#E89A7E'

# Prepare data
dotcom_nasdaq = [(d['quarter_offset'], d['index_value']) for d in data['nasdaq_index']['data'] if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
ai_nasdaq = [(d['quarter_offset'], d['index_value']) for d in data['nasdaq_index']['data'] if d['era'] == 'AI']

dotcom_pe = [(d['quarter_offset'], d['pe']) for d in data['pe_ratio']['data'] if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
ai_pe = [(d['quarter_offset'], d['pe']) for d in data['pe_ratio']['data'] if d['era'] == 'AI']

dotcom_ipo = [(d['year'], d['ipo_count']) for d in data['ipo_counts']['data'] if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
ai_ipo = [(d['year'], d['ipo_count']) for d in data['ipo_counts']['data'] if d['era'] == 'AI']

dotcom_earn = [(d['year'], d['earnings_bn']) for d in data['corporate_earnings']['data'] if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
ai_earn = [(d['year'], d['earnings_bn']) for d in data['corporate_earnings']['data'] if d['era'] == 'AI']

# Map years to quarter offsets
dotcom_start_year = 1997
ai_start_year = 2021

dotcom_ipo_x = [(y - dotcom_start_year) * 4 for y, _ in dotcom_ipo]
dotcom_ipo_y = [v for _, v in dotcom_ipo]
ai_ipo_x = [(y - ai_start_year) * 4 for y, _ in ai_ipo]
ai_ipo_y = [v for _, v in ai_ipo]

dotcom_earn_x = [(y - dotcom_start_year) * 4 for y, _ in dotcom_earn]
dotcom_earn_y = [v for _, v in dotcom_earn]
ai_earn_x = [(y - ai_start_year) * 4 for y, _ in ai_earn]
ai_earn_y = [v for _, v in ai_earn]

# Unpack line data
dc_nas_x, dc_nas_y = zip(*dotcom_nasdaq)
ai_nas_x, ai_nas_y = zip(*dotcom_nasdaq)[:len(ai_nasdaq)]
ai_nas_x2, ai_nas_y2 = zip(*ai_nasdaq)

dc_pe_x, dc_pe_y = zip(*dotcom_pe)
ai_pe_x, ai_pe_y = zip(*ai_pe)

# Create figure with 4 rows, 1 column, shared x-axis
fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 1, figsize=(14, 16), sharex=True, gridspec_kw={'hspace': 0.08})

# Common x-axis setup
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_xlim(-1, 25)
    ax.set_xticks([0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24])
    ax.set_xticklabels(['Year 0\n(Q1)', 'Year 1', 'Year 2', 'Year 3', 'Year 4', 'Year 5', 'Year 6\n(Q1)'])
    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    ax.axvspan(-1, 16.5, alpha=0.03, color='gray')  # AI era background marker

# Panel 1: NASDAQ Index
ax1 = axes[0]
ax1.plot(dc_nas_x, dc_nas_y, color=COLOR_DOTCOM, linewidth=2.5, label='Dot-com (1997–2002)', marker='o', markersize=4, zorder=3)
ax1.plot(ai_nas_x2, ai_nas_y2, color=COLOR_AI, linewidth=2.5, label='AI era (2021–2024)', marker='s', markersize=4, zorder=3)
# Peak markers
ax1.axvline(x=12, color=COLOR_DOTCOM, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.2, alpha=0.6)
ax1.axvline(x=15, color=COLOR_AI, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.2, alpha=0.6)
ax1.annotate('Dot-com peak\nMar 2000', xy=(12, 305.2), xytext=(12, 325),
            fontsize=9, ha='center', color=COLOR_DOTCOM, fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=COLOR_DOTCOM, lw=1))
ax1.annotate('AI-era high\nQ4 2024', xy=(15, 148.7), xytext=(17.5, 165),
            fontsize=9, ha='center', color=COLOR_AI, fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=COLOR_AI, lw=1))
ax1.set_ylabel('NASDAQ Index\n(base = 100)', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_title('NASDAQ Trajectory: Two Tech-Driven Booms Compared', fontsize=14, fontweight='bold', loc='left', pad=10)
ax1.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, fancybox=False, edgecolor='gray')
ax1.set_ylim(60, 350)
ax1.grid(True, axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# Panel 2: P/E Ratio
ax2 = axes[1]
ax2.plot(dc_pe_x, dc_pe_y, color=COLOR_DOTCOM, linewidth=2.5, label='Dot-com', marker='o', markersize=5, zorder=3)
ax2.plot(ai_pe_x, ai_pe_y, color=COLOR_AI, linewidth=2.5, label='AI era', marker='s', markersize=5, zorder=3)
ax2.fill_between(dc_pe_x, dc_pe_y, alpha=0.15, color=COLOR_DOTCOM)
ax2.fill_between(ai_pe_x, ai_pe_y, alpha=0.15, color=COLOR_AI)
# Annotations for peaks
ax2.annotate(f'Peak: {max(dc_pe_y):.1f}x', xy=(12, 105.2), xytext=(9, 115),
            fontsize=9, ha='center', color=COLOR_DOTCOM, fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=COLOR_DOTCOM, lw=1))
ax2.annotate(f'Current: {max(ai_pe_y):.1f}x', xy=(15, 40.3), xytext=(17, 50),
            fontsize=9, ha='center', color=COLOR_AI, fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=COLOR_AI, lw=1))
ax2.set_ylabel('P/E Ratio (x)', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_title('Valuation Extremes: Dot-com P/E Reached ~105×; AI Era Stays Below 41×', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', loc='left', pad=8)
ax2.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, fancybox=False, edgecolor='gray')
ax2.set_ylim(15, 125)
ax2.grid(True, axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# Panel 3: IPO Counts
ax3 = axes[2]
bar_width = 1.2
ax3.bar([x - bar_width/2 for x in dotcom_ipo_x], dotcom_ipo_y, width=bar_width, color=COLOR_DOTCOM, alpha=0.85, label='Dot-com', zorder=3, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
ax3.bar([x + bar_width/2 for x in ai_ipo_x], ai_ipo_y, width=bar_width, color=COLOR_AI, alpha=0.85, label='AI era', zorder=3, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
# Add value labels
for x, y in zip(dotcom_ipo_x, dotcom_ipo_y):
    ax3.text(x - bar_width/2, y + 8, str(y), ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=8.5, color=COLOR_DOTCOM, fontweight='bold')
for x, y in zip(ai_ipo_x, ai_ipo_y):
    ax3.text(x + bar_width/2, y + 8, str(y), ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=8.5, color=COLOR_AI, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_ylabel('Tech IPOs (count)', fontsize=10)
ax3.set_title('IPO Frenzy: Dot-com Saw 308 Listings in 1999 Alone; AI Era Peaked at 198', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', loc='left', pad=8)
ax3.legend(loc='upper right', frameon=True, fancybox=False, edgecolor='gray')
ax3.set_ylim(0, 360)
ax3.grid(True, axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# Panel 4: Corporate Earnings
ax4 = axes[3]
# For earnings, use bars with negative values possible
bars_dc = ax4.bar([x - bar_width/2 for x in dotcom_earn_x], dotcom_earn_y, width=bar_width, color=COLOR_DOTCOM, alpha=0.85, label='Dot-com', zorder=3, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
bars_ai = ax4.bar([x + bar_width/2 for x in ai_earn_x], ai_earn_y, width=bar_width, color=COLOR_AI, alpha=0.85, label='AI era', zorder=3, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5)
# Add value labels
for x, y in zip(dotcom_earn_x, dotcom_earn_y):
    offset = 12 if y >= 0 else -18
    ax4.text(x - bar_width/2, y + offset, f'${y:.1f}B', ha='center', va='bottom' if y >= 0 else 'top', fontsize=8.5, color=COLOR_DOTCOM, fontweight='bold')
for x, y in zip(ai_earn_x, ai_earn_y):
    ax4.text(x + bar_width/2, y + 12, f'${y:.1f}B', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=8.5, color=COLOR_AI, fontweight='bold')
ax4.axhline(y=0, color='black', linewidth=0.8, zorder=2)
ax4.set_ylabel('NASDAQ-100 Earnings\n(billion USD, nominal)', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_title('Earnings Backdrop: AI-era Profits Are an Order of Magnitude Larger and Still Growing', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', loc='left', pad=8)
ax4.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, fancybox=False, edgecolor='gray')
ax4.set_ylim(-50, 600)
ax4.grid(True, axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# X-axis label on bottom panel
ax4.set_xlabel('Years from era start', fontsize=11)

# Add a subtle shared annotation about the AI era ending
fig.text(0.5, 0.01, 'Data: Quarterly NASDAQ Composite, trailing P/E, annual tech IPO counts, and NASDAQ-100 aggregate earnings. AI-era data through Q4 2024.',
         ha='center', fontsize=9, style='italic', color='dimgray')

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.98])

# Add overall figure title
fig.suptitle('Dot-com vs. AI Bubble: Do the Two Eras Share the Same Shape?',
             fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995, ha='left', x=0.02)

plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight', facecolor='white', edgecolor='none')
plt.close()
print("Chart saved to /app/output/result.png")
